audits.title: Screening for gestational diabetes: a retrospective audit.
audits.standard: Diabetic Pregnancy Study Group timed random blood sugar thresholds (fasting >6.1 mmol/l, non-fasting >7.0 mmol/l) compared with local thresholds

cycle1.result: Among women with t-RBS between local and proposed thresholds, 257 (97.7%) had a normal GTT and 6 (2.30%) abnormal; 4 (1.52%) were labelled gestational diabetic, all diet-managed with no adverse outcome.

audits.other_findings: Many GTTs were judged unnecessary and adopting the higher thresholds was recommended; 45 patients had no GTT result.
audits.citation: Kulkarni M, Jones KD, Newbold S. Screening for gestational diabetes: a retrospective audit. J Obstet Gynaecol. 2003;23(2):160-162. doi:10.1080/0144361031000074691. PMID: 12745560.

audits.title: Implementation of new recommendations for the diagnosis of gestational diabetes: a 5-month audit.
audits.standard: International recommendations for gestational diabetes diagnosis (75 g OGTT, fasting glucose threshold 5.1 mmol/L)
audits.intervention: Implementation of new diagnostic criteria (one-step 75 g OGTT).

cycle2.result: 77.0% performed the correct protocol; 38 (15.1%) 75 g OGTTs positive.

audits.other_findings: New recommendations not correctly applied in 23%, mainly ignoring the fasting glucose threshold.
audits.citation: Szoke D, Valente C, Dolci A, Panteghini M. Implementation of new recommendations for the diagnosis of gestational diabetes: a 5-month audit. Clin Chem Lab Med. 2012;50(7):1271-1273. doi:10.1515/cclm.2011.757. PMID: 22007961.

audits.title: [Clinical audit of screening for gestational diabetes among 848 pregnant women in 23 maternity units of the Pays de la Loire, 2014].
audits.standard: 2010 national guidelines for gestational diabetes screening
audits.setting: 23 maternity units of the Pays de la Loire perinatal network

cycle1.period: A week of deliveries in June 2014
cycle1.result: Adherence to screening guidelines 45.5%, non-adherence 27.6%, over-screening 26.9%; OGTT performed per guidelines in 95.9%; specialist follow-up of GDM 84.6%.

audits.other_findings: GDM diagnosed in 14.6%; network plans repeated dissemination of guidelines and chart review sessions.
audits.citation: Branger B, Velupillai C, François S, Coutin AS, Paumier A, Gillard P, et al.. [Clinical audit of screening for gestational diabetes among 848 pregnant women in 23 maternity units of the Pays de la Loire, 2014]. J Gynecol Obstet Biol Reprod (Paris). 2016;45(8):876-889. doi:10.1016/j.jgyn.2016.02.011. PMID: 27068754.

audits.title: Diabetes screening in pregnancy failing women in rural Western Australia: An audit of oral glucose tolerance test completion rates.
audits.standard: Screening for gestational diabetes with OGTT in second or third trimester
audits.setting: Rural and remote antenatal services, Western Australia

cycle1.result: 278 (50.5%) screened with OGTT; 113 (20.5%) had no record of any GDM screening.

audits.other_findings: Aboriginal women were less likely to be screened; GDM rate 14.7% among those screened vs 7.4% state-wide.
audits.citation: Kirke AB, Atkinson D, Moore S, Sterry K, Singleton S, Roxburgh C, et al.. Diabetes screening in pregnancy failing women in rural Western Australia: An audit of oral glucose tolerance test completion rates. Aust J Rural Health. 2019;27(1):64-69. doi:10.1111/ajr.12465. PMID: 30693987.

audits.title: An Audit of Pre-Pregnancy Maternal Obesity and Diabetes Screening in Rural Regional Tasmania and Its Impact on Pregnancy and Neonatal Outcomes.
audits.standard: Recommended gestational weight gain standards and oral glucose tolerance test screening
audits.setting: Rural and regional Tasmania, maternity digital records

cycle1.result: 55% overweight or obese; 43.6% gained above recommended weight; 35.8% did not have an oral glucose tolerance test.

audits.other_findings: Obesity and low screening were associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes.
audits.citation: Luccisano SP, Weber HC, Murfet GO, Robertson IK, Prior SJ, Hills AP. An Audit of Pre-Pregnancy Maternal Obesity and Diabetes Screening in Rural Regional Tasmania and Its Impact on Pregnancy and Neonatal Outcomes. Int J Environ Res Public Health. 2021;18(22):12006. doi:10.3390/ijerph182212006. PMID: 34831762.

audits.title: Adherence to gestational diabetes screening guidelines: Retrospective audit in three public hospitals in Ethiopia.
audits.standard: Guideline-recommended universal GDM screening at 24-28 weeks
audits.setting: Antenatal care in three public hospitals, Addis Ababa

cycle1.result: 139/1050 (13.2%) screened for GDM; only 8.6% of screened women tested in the recommended 24-28 week window; median gestational age at screening 34 weeks [IQR 30-37]; 99.3% risk-based screening

audits.other_findings: OGTT was the main method (87.8%); 57/139 (41.0%) screened women were diagnosed with GDM. Screening was associated with hospital site, older age, higher parity and earlier first antenatal visit.
audits.citation: Roro MA, Amogne MT, Gebre MW, Rhodes EC, Johnson LCM, Gary R, et al.. Adherence to gestational diabetes screening guidelines: Retrospective audit in three public hospitals in Ethiopia. PLoS One. 2026;21(8):e0357102. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0357102. PMID: 42640935.
